keys.description: the admin secret admin-api holds (ADMIN_API_TOKEN). meeting-api never signs with it directly: the MeetingToken key is derived from it as HMAC-SHA256(ADMIN_TOKEN, "vexa/meeting-token/v1") (meeting_token.signing_key), which HS256-signs the per-spawn MeetingToken AND verifies the lifecycle callback, the recordings upload and the transcript stream entries; unset, every POST /bots would 500, so the boot refuses instead (A4). A PUBLISHED PLACEHOLDER is refused on the same terms as INTERNAL_API_SECRET: the literal is in this repository, so anyone can forge a MeetingToken and upload a recording against any meeting (A19). The list is the internal-secret placeholders plus every default and example this repository has shipped for the admin key on any surface (compose, Helm, Lite, CI, docs); it is held equal to admin-api's ADMIN_API_TOKEN and flows' VEXA_FLOWS_ADMIN_KEY by fact admin-token-placeholders.

the runtime caller credential meeting-api presents (`Authorization: Bearer`) on every runtime.v1 call — bot spawns, liveness probes, teardown. The runtime refuses any other caller; the same value is set on the runtime and on agent-api, and never placed in a bot invocation. Unset, the boot refuses: every POST /bots would be refused by the runtime

gateway-identity.v1 verification key: a file holding the gateway's Ed25519 PUBLIC key (SubjectPublicKeyInfo PEM). meeting-api rebuilds every x-user-* header (owner, bot limit, workspace memberships, webhook) from a verified signature and refuses (401) one that is neither signed nor carried by the internal tier. It verifies and cannot sign; a private key in this file refuses the boot, as does a missing file or any other key type. Generated at install with the gateway's signing key: compose's identity-keys one-shot, the Helm identity-keys ConfigMap, the Lite entrypoint
PostgreSQL host (the meeting/session/transcript store)
PostgreSQL port
PostgreSQL database name
PostgreSQL user

PostgreSQL password. No default: unset, the boot refuses. `postgres`, the value every unconfigured stack once shared, and the other values published in this repository are refused the same way, as compose's postgres service refuses them
explicit async SQLAlchemy URL override; when unset the URL is built from the DB_* parts (lite deliberately sets only DB_* so the asyncpg driver is chosen). DB_PASSWORD is required at boot either way

SQLAlchemy async-engine pool_size (persistent connections per pod) applied at every engine site via meeting_api.db.build_engine. Pure runtime override — reconcile with deploy/db-budget.json (Σ replicas × (pool_size + max_overflow) + reserved ≤ max_connections) on managed Postgres. #635.
SQLAlchemy async-engine max_overflow (burst connections above pool_size per pod). Pure runtime override — reconcile with deploy/db-budget.json. #635.
the transcription_segments stream + bm:meeting:{id}:status pub/sub + bot-command channel backing

how often (s) meeting-api checks whether Redis is a new process (one INFO) and, when it is, defines again every bot Redis user — Redis keeps none across a restart, so a live bot's credential would otherwise stay refused until its meeting ended

what a spawned meeting bot connects to Redis as. `per-workload`: a Redis user of its own — append to transcription_segments, its own meeting's live-update and command channels — defined at spawn and removed when it ends; the service connection never reaches it. `shared`: the service connection, for a Redis that cannot define users (some managed services); every meeting bot can then read and write every other's keys, so it is safe only where every person on the instance trusts every other. The service's own Redis user needs ACL SETUSER/DELUSER for `per-workload`.
the runtime kernel's runtime.v1 surface bot_spawn creates workloads on

this service's own base URL as the spawned bot must reach it (lifecycle.v1 callback + transcript socket); compose relies on the default service DNS name, helm sets it explicitly to the release-qualified Service DNS, lite overrides to localhost

keys.default: (unset — no internal-tier caller is admitted, and none may name a person)
keys.description: shared secret for internal service-to-service calls: meeting-api presents it on admin-api's internal routes and admits it (from trusted services, never from a bot — a bot holds only its session's MeetingToken) on the bot lifecycle callback and the recording upload, and it is the internal tier gateway-identity.v1 believes an unsigned X-User-Id from (agent-api acting for a person). Unset is a documented degrade; a PUBLISHED PLACEHOLDER is not — it is the whole internal tier handed to anyone who read the repository (F95), so the boot refuses it.
server-side bot participant name used by POST /bots when bot_name is omitted
STT base URL the spawned bot transcribes against (the client appends /v1/audio/transcriptions) — self-hosted deploy/transcription or a hosted vexa.ai token's endpoint
bearer token for the STT service (must match that unit's API_TOKEN)

STT model id bot_spawn threads into the invocation (the OpenAI-compatible `model` form part) — required by backends that validate model ids (Groq, vLLM); ignored by the bundled deploy/transcription unit. Helm plumbing is a declared follow-up (deploy/helm/README.md) — use extraEnv there for now
deployment-level default for a spawn's transcribe_enabled when the request does not say — set false for a capture-only deployment with no STT

Comma-separated additional Jitsi deployment hostnames (a self-hosted instance whose name carries neither 'jitsi' nor a 'meet' label, e.g. calls.example.org) recognized when parsing pasted meeting links AND calendar (ICS) links; meet.jit.si, *jitsi* hosts, and (for pasted links) meet-labelled hosts are always recognized — unset ⇒ no extra hosts
deployment-level default for a spawn's recording_enabled when the request does not say

deployment-scoped authenticated-bot knob: when true, EVERY POST /bots spawn carries the invocation.v1 auth block so the bot restores the provisioned browser session (make login) and joins signed-in. Demands the BOT_USERDATA_S3_PATH + BOT_S3_* keys — incomplete config answers a typed 503 (never a silent anonymous join).

keys.default: (unset — required when BOT_AUTHENTICATED=true; the userdata prefix holding the provisioned session, e.g. userdata/bot-identity-1)
keys.description: stored-session prefix; also the per-identity serialization key (one live authenticated bot per prefix)
userdata store endpoint, reachable from the bot containers (each restores its session from it) and from meeting-api (which writes an authenticated bot's session back to it), e.g. http://minio:9000
userdata store bucket

READ-ONLY userdata-store access key (Get + List on the userdata prefix): it rides the invocation env into the bot container, and the bot only restores with it. Never a storage root key: meeting-api refuses an authenticated spawn, and the session write-back, when this pair shares a half with a storage root pair (S3_* / MINIO_*)
read-only userdata-store secret key (see BOT_S3_ACCESS_KEY)
object-store host:port (or full http(s) URL) recordings are written to
object-store access key: recordings upload/finalize, and the authenticated bot's session write-back to the userdata store
object-store secret key
recordings bucket
https toward the object store when true
explicit S3 endpoint override for a non-MinIO store; helm sets it from storage.s3.endpoint
explicit S3 access-key override, for recordings and the authenticated bot's session write-back; helm reads it from the storage.s3.existingSecret Secret
explicit S3 secret-key override; helm reads it from the storage.s3.existingSecret Secret
recordings bucket for the standalone recordings composition (the unified app uses MINIO_BUCKET first)
storage-backend label stamped into the recording's meeting.data JSONB; helm sets s3
boto3's shared-config file, read by the recordings S3 client (not by meeting-api code); helm points it at a mounted file carrying storage.s3's signing region, addressing style and CA bundle
MeetingToken lifetime — must outlive the bot's max active time (default 4h) or transcription dies mid-meeting
poll interval (s) of the transcription_segments stream consumer loop
db-writer cadence (seconds) — each tick flushes immutable live segments from the redis hash meeting:{id}:segments into the transcriptions table (the restored 0.10 flush loop)
parent-name alias for DB_WRITER_INTERVAL_S (0.10 collector env parity) — used only when DB_WRITER_INTERVAL_S is unset

how often (seconds) the db-writer runs its self-healing O(keyspace) meeting:*:segments SCAN — startup + every this-many seconds, off the DB_WRITER_INTERVAL_S hot path. The active_meetings set is authoritative in steady state; the per-tick scan saturated redis and starved /health, restarting healthy pods (#893)

how long (seconds) the db-writer keeps re-draining a FINISHED meeting's copilot processed-notes stream while waiting for the producing worker's view_end marker, before giving up loudly. The copilot's final beat runs ~10s after session_end and by then the meeting has left the active sweep, so without the parked re-drain those last notes stay in redis forever (ADR 0027)
seconds a live segment must sit unmodified before the db-writer flushes it to postgres — the still-mutable tail (drafts being refined) stays in redis until it settles (0.10 parity)

the hold (seconds) for a CONFIRMED Teams CSRC segment (source=merged plus speaker_key=csrc:<id>), whose drafts are explicitly retractable. Never raises the hold above IMMUTABILITY_THRESHOLD; pending Teams rows and every other lane keep the full hold
TTL (seconds) re-armed on the live segment hash meeting:{id}:segments at every append — an abandoned hash cannot linger forever once flushed (0.10 parity)
sweep interval (s) of the webhook retry-queue drain loop
tick interval (s) of the schedule.v1 job loop (drives join-retry re-spawns)
grace (s) before a stopping meeting whose workload is gone is reconciled
interval (s) of the stop-reconcile loop
grace (s) before an active meeting with a dead workload is failed by the reconciler

grace (s) before a meeting whose bot has NOT yet reached the room (requested/joining/awaiting_admission) is reconciled — DERIVED from the lobby budget the spawn issues (VEXA_LOBBY_BUDGET_S, default 900s) plus 60s of headroom, so the control plane is never less patient than the deadline it handed the bot (#862, #1208)

lobby budget (s) issued to every spawned bot as automatic_leave.waitingRoomTimeout — how long it may wait for admission before reporting awaiting_admission_timeout. 15 min so an auto-joined bot outwaits a late host (#1208); the reconcile pre-active grace derives from it, so raising it never leaves a waiter reaped by a shorter watchdog. An explicit automatic_leave.max_wait_for_admission on POST /bots still wins.
continuous-untracked window (s): a meeting whose workload the runtime 404s for this long with no re-adoption and no bot callback is presumed lost and failed with an evidence note

JSON service-authority.v1 adapter config: credential-free endpoint URL, contract_version, timeout_ms, response_max_age_seconds, failure_policy=closed, and mode=enforce|observe. When set, unavailable or malformed authority decisions fail closed.
shared HMAC secret for exact-byte timestamped service-authority requests
poll cadence for due one-minute active-service decisions; boundary timestamps remain admitted_at + N minutes regardless of polling cadence

Boot-frozen operator destination for signed meeting.completed and bot.failed envelopes. It is never read from user or meeting data. HTTPS is required unless VEXA_SYSTEM_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_HTTP explicitly enables an in-cluster HTTP service.
Shared secret for Bearer compatibility and exact-byte timestamped HMAC signing of the operator-owned terminal callback.
Explicit operator opt-in for an HTTP system callback on a private/in-cluster service network. This never changes the customer webhook SSRF policy.
Bounded HTTP timeout in seconds for the operator-owned terminal callback; must be greater than 0 and at most 60.
uvicorn bind host (lite binds 127.0.0.1 behind its internal proxy)
uvicorn bind port
uvicorn/app log level

keys.default: (unset — calendar sync no-ops and the auto-join sweep cannot resolve the per-user cap, so it fails closed and refuses to spawn unless AUTO_JOIN_ALLOW_UNCAPPED=1)
keys.description: admin-api base URL for the internal edges the background sweeps call (/internal/users/{id}/bot-context, /internal/calendar-configs). Required on every deploy surface so calendar sync runs and auto-join spawns stay capped (#656).
auto-join sweep cadence (s) — how often scheduled meetings are checked for a due start
auto-join lead (s) — the bot is sent this long before data.scheduled_at, so it is standing in the lobby at the scheduled start rather than setting out then (#1208). Deploy values may override.
auto-join grace (s) — a scheduled meeting older than this is never auto-joined (no hours-late joins)
backoff (s) before an auto-join that failed loudly (cap/quota/spawn) is retried

keys.default: false — with no admin edge (ADMIN_API_URL/INTERNAL_API_SECRET) the per-user cap is unresolvable and the sweep fails closed (refuses to spawn); set 1 to deliberately allow uncapped self-host spawns
keys.description: opt-in escape hatch (#656): allow the auto-join sweep to spawn uncapped when the per-user cap cannot be resolved. Unsafe mode — chosen, never defaulted.
calendar-sync sweep cadence (s) — how often connected ICS feeds are re-fetched and upserted into planned meetings
#527: a background loop whose last heartbeat is older than this flips /health to degraded+503 (a hung consumer no longer looks alive)
#527: collector-group lag (unread transcription_segments) over this flips /health to degraded+503
#527: acked transcription_segments entries older than this are trimmed; an unread (un-acked) entry is NEVER trimmed regardless of age (the 2026-04-26 data-loss guard)
#636: per-replica Redis consumer name for the segment group; empty → derived as collector-<hostname> (pod identity) so a crashed replica's pending batch is attributable + reclaimable

#660: idle (ms) after which an abandoned per-recreate consumer (pending==0) is pruned from collector_group by the reclaim sweep (XGROUP DELCONSUMER); default 30 min, well above COLLECTOR_RECLAIM_MIN_IDLE_MS so a briefly-quiet live replica is never removed
#636: min idle (ms) before a replica reclaims another replica's un-acked segment batch via XAUTOCLAIM, so a live peer's in-flight batch is never stolen
#636: run the orphan-reclaim scan every N segment-consumer ticks
#636: /health degrades to 503 when the segment group's pending-entry (PEL) depth exceeds this — a stuck/orphaned batch is a reportable state (P18)

O-TEL-1: the captured-signal tape KEEP budget in bytes. Fixture collection is default ON, so the bound lives here rather than on the capture path — the janitor evicts oldest-unpromoted tapes under the `signal/` prefix until total tape bytes fit. Promoted tapes (a PROMOTED marker object beside them) are NEVER evicted; if promotion alone exceeds the budget the sweep deletes nothing and logs signal_tape_budget_unreclaimable for a human to decide
O-TEL-1: captured-signal budget sweep cadence (s) — one paginated listing of the `signal/` prefix plus per-object deletes, single-flighted across replicas
O-TEL-1: minimum tape age (s) before the budget janitor may evict it — the in-flight-upload guard, so a sweep firing mid-teardown can never half-delete a tape whose parts are still arriving

whether a bot tapes its raw captured signal (audio, captions, speaker events) to the bucket under signal/ when identity gives no answer for its owner (unreachable, or an admin-api that predates the field). admin-api reads the same key as its last tier (user > platform setting > this), so a reachable identity already carries it. Unset or empty = true, the compose and Lite behaviour; the Helm chart sets it from diagnostics.captureSignal, default false. Anything but a recognized boolean (true/1/yes/on, false/0/no/off) refuses the boot: whether meetings are taped is a data-protection decision a typo must not make.

flows' intake, told when a bot this service dispatched goes active and when it completes (F168/F181 — an ad hoc bot started via the MCP request_meeting_bot never reached flows before this; only invite_intake's own emit_started/emit_completed, calendar-only, ever did). MEETING-API TELLS FLOWS; IT DOES NOT ASK IT — best-effort, bounded at 2s, swallowed (events.py), so a deployment with no flows domain runs meetings exactly as one with a flows domain does, and so does one where flows is down. Unset is a profile, not a degraded state. Spelled VEXA_FLOWS_API_URL to match agent-api's control_plane/config.v1.json (identity's admin-api spells the bare key FLOWS_API_URL for the same edge — the two publishers that already exist do not agree with each other; not fixed here).

operator key for the same edge, sent as X-Flows-Operator-Key (flows' POST /events is authenticated). Declared as part of the edge rather than beside it, on the same terms as identity's admin-api and agent-api's control_plane declare theirs: unset alongside an unset URL is the no-flows profile; unset with a URL set is a deployment whose facts are being refused.

stt.description: spawned bots can transcribe (the STT service bot_spawn threads into the invocation.v1 payload)
stt.when_unconfigured: POST /bots with transcribe_enabled=true answers a typed 503 naming the unset key(s) — bots must opt out explicitly (transcribe_enabled=false / TRANSCRIBE_ENABLED=false) to spawn capture-only

object_storage.description: recordings persist to the object store (chunk upload + finalize → meeting.data JSONB)
object_storage.when_unconfigured: recording upload/finalize fails at request time with a storage auth error; transcripts are unaffected
